create.name: Cara Barker
create.bio:
Cara Lee Barker is an American Jungian analyst, author and artist based in Kirkland, Washington. She first trained as a nurse, serving in an army nursing programme during the Vietnam era and going on to qualify as a nurse practitioner, then took a doctorate in clinical psychology and studied expressive arts and the body-centred Hakomi method with Ron Kurtz. Her post-doctoral training was at the C.G. Jung Institute in Zurich, and she has taught in the psychology department at Seattle University.

She calls her approach the Way of Soul: learning to trust the guidance that turns up in dreams, in the body, in meaningful coincidences and in creative work, so that loss and upheaval can become a doorway to a fuller life. She leads Way of Soul retreats of three to five days, set up by a sponsoring group at home or abroad, which combine meditation and mindful creative practice with rest. Her books include Heart-Led Living, a guide to finding direction through dreams, body signals and synchronicity, Nightlight, World Weary Woman and The Love Project. Her site also gathers a set of Love Projects, among them one named for Sandy Hook sibling survivors, and she paints; a retrospective of her art was shown in Kirkland in 2016.

books.title: Heart-Led Living: The 4 Cornerstones to Building a Better Life
books.author: Cara Barker
books.description: A practical guide for times of change, built around four foundations for deciding what comes next. Through stories and exercises it shows readers how to draw guidance from their dreams, the signals of the body and chance events that feel meaningful.

books.title: Nightlight: Soul Calling, Body Listening, Heart Speaking
books.author: Cara Barker
books.description: A book for readers worn down by a turbulent world who are looking for rest and inner steadiness. She invites them to find their own small light in dark times by listening to the soul, the body and the heart.

courses.title: The Way of Soul Retreats
courses.description: Private retreats of three, four or five days that she leads for a group whose sponsor handles bookings and logistics, in the United States or abroad. Days combine meditation, mindfulness brought into creative activity, rest and renewal.
